record.paper_title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations: numerical results for the heat semigroup and open questions on them (with appendix: full list of pictures and Python code)
record.context_brief: Chernoff rates below known regularity hypotheses
record.original_question: Let UC_b(R) be the Banach space of bounded uniformly continuous real functions with the sup norm, and let Lf=f'' generate the heat semigroup e^{tL}. Existing rate theorems for Chernoff approximations require smoothness and domain conditions, such as membership in powers of D(L). If those conditions fail, for example when an initial condition f is differentiable only once but not twice and f' is Hölder continuous with exponent 1/2, what is the asymptotic convergence rate of C(t/n)^n f to e^{tL}f as n tends to infinity? More generally, how does the rate depend on the smoothness of f and on whether the Chernoff function C has first-order or higher-order Chernoff tangency to L when f is not in the regularity class covered by the known theorem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Banach space of bounded uniformly continuous functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the supremum norm $\|f\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|f(x)|$. Let $L$ be the closed operator on $UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ defined by $Lf=f''$ on its natural domain $D(L)=\{f\in UC_b(\mathbb{R}): f''\in UC_b(\mathbb{R})\}$. Then $L$ generates the heat semigroup $(e^{tL})_{t\ge 0}$ on $UC_b(\mathbb{R})$, given by 
$$(e^{tL}f)(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi t}}\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{-(x-y)^2/(4t)}f(y)\,dy,\qquad t>0.$$

A strongly continuous family of bounded linear operators $(C(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ with $C(0)=I$ is called a Chernoff function of order $k\ge 1$ tangent to $L$ if for every $f\in D(L^k)$,
$$C(t)f = f + tLf + \tfrac{t^2}{2!}L^2 f + \cdots + \tfrac{t^k}{k!}L^k f + o(t^k)\quad\text{as }t\to 0^+,$$
together with the standard Chernoff hypotheses ensuring $C(t/n)^n f\to e^{tL}f$ in $UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ for every $f\in UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ as $n\to\infty$.

Known rate theorems guarantee, for fixed $t>0$ and $f\in D(L^k)$, that
$$\|C(t/n)^n f - e^{tL}f\|_\infty = O(n^{-k})\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.$$

Now consider $f\in UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ such that $f$ is once continuously differentiable with $f'\in UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ Hölder continuous of exponent $1/2$, but $f\notin D(L)$ (i.e.\ $f''$ does not exist as an element of $UC_b(\mathbb{R})$).

(a) Determine the asymptotic rate of convergence of $\|C(t/n)^n f - e^{tL}f\|_\infty$ as $n\to\infty$, for $t>0$ fixed, when $C$ has first-order Chernoff tangency to $L$.

(b) More generally, for $f\in UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ whose smoothness is described by a Hölder/Sobolev-type modulus weaker than membership in $D(L^k)$, determine how the asymptotic rate of $\|C(t/n)^n f - e^{tL}f\|_\infty$ depends jointly on the smoothness of $f$ and on the order of Chernoff tangency $k$ of $C$ to $L$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of the convergence rate of Chernoff approximations to the heat semigroup for initial conditions outside the standard regularity classes (e.g., $f\notin D(L)$ with only Hölder-regular first derivative) appears still open. Recent works on Chernoff approximations (e.g., upper/lower estimates in the Chernoff product formula, 2024 Israel J. Math.; convergence rates for convex monotone semigroups, 2025) provide rates under regularity assumptions but do not settle the precise asymptotic rate in the low-regularity regime described.

status_evidence.title: Upper and lower estimates for rate of convergence in the Chernoff product formula for semigroups of operators
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes upper and lower bounds for Chernoff product convergence rates under regularity assumptions on the vector.
status_evidence.claim: Recent rate results require regularity (powers of the domain), consistent with the open low-regularity question.

status_evidence.title: Convergence rates for Chernoff-type approximations of convex monotone semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Provides explicit convergence rates depending on smoothness/Hölder regularity of initial data for convex monotone semigroups.
status_evidence.claim: Rate-dependence on smoothness is being actively investigated; the linear heat-semigroup case with low regularity is not definitively resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Speed of convergence of Chernoff approximations for two model examples
status_evidence.snippet: Studies convergence rates of Chernoff approximations for the heat and transport equations as model examples.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the question of rates for various smoothness classes remains an active area without complete resolution.
